sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Ultra-HD 4K Minimally Invasive Rigid Endoscopes

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified tradition rooted in Spanish and Argentine models, with United States-influenced commercial statutes and a separate foundation law of Anglo-Caribbean trust inspiration)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Ley 13 de 1997 and Ley 32 de 2016; Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT Framework Law); Decreto Ley 2 de 2010, as amended by Decreto Ley 1 de 2011, establishing the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the non-financial regulated subjects regime; Ley 70 de 29 de octubre de 2019 establishing the central Beneficial Ownership Registry with restricted government access; implementing regulations and administrative resolutions of the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SSRF); and the due-diligence circulars issued by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) and the Dirección Nacional de Sujetos No Financieros.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the founder's valid passport or national photo identification document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry, consulate, or notarial authority in the founder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a contracting state to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, in force since 30 November 1991); consular legalization at the Panamanian embassy or consulate for instruments originating in non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original banker's reference letter confirming the founder's account history, reputation, and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or regulated financial institution holding the founder's accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, together with a Spanish translation certified by a Panamanian translator where required by the resident agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Panamanian resident agent and recognizing counsel to execute the foundation charter and public deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or consul in the founder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with Spanish translation included in the notarial protocol of the Panama notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or equivalent corporate existence evidence for non-natural-person founders and corporate officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry or competent public authority in the entity's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; issuer's digital verification code accepted where the registries participate in the Panama Public Registry's international interoperability network

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of each founder, council member, initial beneficiary, and legal representative against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, FATF public statements, INTERPOL red notices, and Panama's domestic UAF and Public Registry watchlists. PEP determination follows the definition in Ley 23 de 2015 and SBP regulations, requiring enhanced due diligence, documented source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, and senior-management approval for any PEP or high-risk jurisdiction connection. Negative screening results must be documented in the resident agent's AML file and retained for five years after termination of the professional relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Sede Electrónica (online name search and reservation module administered by the Foundation Section or Mercantile Books Directorate, as applicable)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names may be in Spanish or any language transliterated in Latin script; registration requires a Spanish translation of the foundation charter when drafted in a foreign language, and the registered name must be phonetically and graphically distinguishable from existing entries. The name need not include the word 'Fundación' but the use of a distinguishing suffix is standard practice and avoids confusion with commercial companies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the resident agent will receive an official note identifying the conflicting entry or prohibited token. The resident agent shall file a written reconsideration request (recurso de reconsideración) with the Registrar of the Foundation Section within five (5) business days of notification, submitting supporting evidence such as a permission letter from the Superintendency of Banks or the relevant ministry for sensitive tokens, or documentation of prior authorized use. If the reconsideration is denied, the resident agent may file an administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Dirección General of the Registro Público de Panamá within ten (10) business days. In parallel, the applicant may reserve two or three alternative names to avoid delaying the incorporation timetable; a confirmed denial can also be challenged before the competent administrative litigation chamber of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within the statutory period, although alternative-name reservation is the commercially preferred remedy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A private interest foundation is required to designate a resident agent in Panama who maintains the registered office (oficina registrada); the resident agent's physical office satisfies the registered-office obligation and a dedicated administrative virtual office is acceptable for the foundation's day-to-day file management, board communications, and record-keeping. A virtual office without any local substance is not sufficient if the foundation conducts regulated, licensing-dependent, or physical manufacturing activities in Panama; for the present ISIC 3250 medical-device manufacturing scope, a physical premises and local operational substance must be established if domestic production is contemplated, while a purely passive ownership holding of foreign operating subsidiaries may lawfully be administered remotely through the resident agent.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: annualized probability of an unannounced inspection of the resident-agent registered office is estimated at below 10% for a low-risk foundation holding foreign assets; however, the SSRF conducts programmatic AML compliance inspections of resident agents rather than foundation premises. If the foundation elects to operate a manufacturing plant for surgical endoscopes in Panama, unannounced on-site inspections by the Ministry of Health (MINSA) under Decree No. 671 de 1984 and municipal fire and safety authorities can occur with an estimated annual probability of 30%, and the UAF may conduct targeted inspections in connection with trade-based money laundering or customs verification of medical-device exports.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foundation name search and official name reservation certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff fixed by the Public Registry fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the foundation charter, reglamento interno (private regulations), and organizational resolutions in Spanish and English
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for multinational private client work

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the public deed before a Panamanian notary and inscription of the foundation at the Public Registry, including all protocol and inscription stamps
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaría designada y Registro Público de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial and registry tariff, plus disbursement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of founder identification, banker's reference, and corporate good-standing documents, including Spanish certified translation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministerio de Gobierno de Panamá (apostille unit), foreign Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for apostille (USD 40 per document) plus foreign consular fees and professional translation fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent acceptance service and registered office provision for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (USD 500-600 per annum for a foundation with no local operations)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC and PEP/sanctions due-diligence bundle covering the foundation's founder, council members, initial beneficiaries, and intended economic sectors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Resident agent compliance department / external AML consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for risk assessment, source-of-funds review, and screening report

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial ownership declaration preparation and preliminary filing support for the Ley 70 de 2019 register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: SSRF plus administrative handling fee of the registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for specialized UBO filing and legal opinion on disclosure levels

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), Articles 1-19, as amended by Ley 82 de 2013 and related provisions of the Reglamento del Registro Público (Decreto 293 de 1996). In subsidiary matters, the Ley General de Sociedades (Law 32 of 1927) applies by analogy under Article 1, final paragraph.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundation Section), Archivo General de las Américas, Ancón, Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (public deed of incorporation of a private interest foundation), executed before a Panamanian Notary Public and recorded in the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Foundation must maintain a minimum initial endowment (patrimonio) of USD 10,000.00 or equivalent asset value. There is no statutory escrow account requirement; the endowment must be expressly stated and contributed in the Public Deed, and the Foundation Council must document receipt in the Foundation's records before commencing business operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: This First Board Resolution of the Private Interest Foundation (the 'Foundation') is adopted on [date] and resolves as follows: (1) the Founder's initial endowment of USD 10,000 is accepted and recorded as the Foundation's patrimony; (2) the registered office is adopted at the Resident Agent's address in Panama City, Panama, for statutory service of process; (3) the Foundation Council is appointed with full fiduciary administration authority; (4) the President and Secretary are elected, authorized to open bank accounts, execute the Foundation Deed, and file all registry and tax registrations; (5) the Bylaws and Beneficiary Statement are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of licensed Resident Agent and reservation of the Foundation name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Resident Agent (attorney-at-law or fiduciary licensed under Ley 25 de 1995, supervised under the AML/CFT regime)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conclude a Resident Agent engagement agreement with a licensed Panamanian attorney or fiduciary. Provide passport, source-of-funds declaration, Council membership and beneficiary information. The Resident Agent verifies KYC and requests availability of the proposed Foundation name from the Public Registry Foundation Section. If the name is available, the Resident Agent issues a name reservation and integrates it into the draft deed.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Founder's passport and secondary identification
Bank or professional reference letters under AML due diligence
Beneficiary and Foundation Council identification sheet
Name availability check request
Resident Agent engagement agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged, the Resident Agent files an alternative name on the same client file the same business day; appeal in writing to the Director General of the Public Registry is available but re-filing the alternative name is the faster cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation before the Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público de la República de Panamá (First Notarial District of the Province of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder (or its attorney-in-fact) and the appointed Foundation Council appear before the Notary Public. The notary reads the final Escritura Pública containing the Foundation name, purpose (manufacture of surgical endoscopy devices and laparoscopy towers, ISIC 3250), endowment, registered office, Resident Agent, Council members and beneficiary information. The parties initial and sign every page; the notary protocolizes and issues the first certified copy.
required_dossiers: Final draft of the Escritura Pública
Resident Agent appointment certificate
AML/KYC file of the Founder, Council and Beneficiaries
Name reservation confirmation
Valid identification documents of all appearing parties
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any notarial observation (e.g., incomplete legalization of a foreign signature or deficient beneficiary instrument) is cured by executing an addendum protocolizado or by resubmitting corrected identification without challenging the notary's decision; a second appearance day typically suffices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Foundation in the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Ancón, Panama City)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original notarial certified copy and three additional copies of the Escritura Pública, together with the Registry application form and tariff voucher. The Registry reviews the legality of the deed, verifies the Resident Agent license and endowment clause, and enters the Foundation under a unique Ficha and an Inscripción number. The certified registration certificate confers legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarial first certified copy of the Escritura Pública
Registry tariff receipt
Registration cover letter signed by the Resident Agent
Three plain copies of the deed
Passport or RUC evidence of the Founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a preventive inscription notice, the Resident Agent renders the requested clarifications (e.g., endowment clause or notarial legalization) within 30 days in the same case file; correction does not require a new full tariff, only a minor deficiency fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and municipal registration of the Foundation and the industrial establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipio de Panamá, Tesorería Municipal or the corresponding district municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Foundation with DGI to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) and, where applicable, an employer RUC for the manufacturing workforce. File the municipal aviso de operación under activity code 3250, present the lease or ownership title of the plant premises, and obtain the municipal operation certificate. Concurrently, prepare the MICI industrial license application to permit local manufacturing activities.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Foundation deed
Photo identification of Council members and authorized signatories
DGI Form 201 corporate tax registration
Municipal commercial establishment application and lease title
Annual municipal patent payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI assigns a provisional fiscal category or the municipality applies a different activity code, a written rectification citing the Foundation's objects and ISIC 3250 is filed within 10 working days; reclassification is normally effective retroactively from the aviso date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate banking account opening for SWIFT LC and TT wire rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá licensed commercial banks (including Banco Nacional de Panamá and private banks offering treasury services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the registered Foundation documents to the chosen bank, complete the Beneficial Ownership form, and provide the board resolution designating signatories. The bank verifies the Registry status and the Resident Agent certificate, then activates SWIFT LC and T/T transfer capabilities for import and export settlements.
required_dossiers: Registry inscription certificate
Foundation Deed and Council Regulations with current Council minutes
Board resolution opening the account
RUC certificate of the Foundation
Beneficial Ownership and source of funds declaration of the Founder
Reference letters for all signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional economic substance proof, file a supplementary lease, payroll projection or purchase order for the endoscopy plant; there is no statutory administrative appeal for refusal, so a second licensed bank is selected with a fully prepared file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of the First Board Resolution and maintenance of statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council of the Private Interest Foundation, with records kept at the Resident Agent's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the Council with all members present or represented, adopt the First Board Resolution, and obtain the Resident Agent's registered office certificate. Open the statutory books, including the register of Council resolutions and the registry of beneficiaries, and maintain the Foundation's financial records under the pragmatic records regime permitted by the Private Interest Foundation Law.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution minutes signed by Council members
Council members' consents
Registered Office certificate from the Resident Agent
Statutory ledger for Council resolutions
Updated Beneficiary Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a Council member contests the contents, a supplemental majority resolution is executed at a second meeting within 5 days and notarized; an omission in the Beneficiary Registry is cured by amending the Beneficiary Statement through the Resident Agent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección General de Industrias (industrial operation certificate), jointly with Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) - Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas (medical device sanitary registration); the manufacturing plant additionally requires a municipal aviso de operación from the relevant Municipality.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario de Dispositivos Médicos (medical device sanitary registration) for Class II/III surgical laparoscopy towers, plus the MICI Certificado de Operación Industrial and the municipal Aviso de Operación de Establecimiento.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Manufacture of rigid endoscopes and laparoscopy towers is classified as a Category II project (moderate environmental impact) under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 2009 and applicable MiAMBIENTE guideline lists when the plant integrates sterilization, metal-finishing or wastewater-generating cleaning lines. A dry assembly and packing operation with no effluent or hazardous air emissions may be classified Category I, subject only to an environmental risk characterization and registration rather than a full EIA study.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater (rinsing, degreasing, cooling) must comply with MiAMBIENTE Resolution No. AG-0847-2015 discharge thresholds (pH 6-9, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, COD ≤ 200 mg/L, TSS ≤ 100 mg/L, oils and greases ≤ 20 mg/L). Air emissions from ethylene oxide, glutaraldehyde sterilization units or vacuum pumps must meet the national air quality and VOC residual standards applicable to medical device manufacturing, with scrubber or catalytic abatement where regulated floor limits are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Visto Bueno de Seguridad of the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (fire safety certificate) after physical inspection of the assembly floor, sterilization vaults and emergency exits; municipal structural load inspection certificate for the manufacturing mezzanine and heavy equipment areas; and the MITRADEL occupational health and workplace clearance certificate covering machine guards, electrical bonding, noise control and ergonomic measures at the laparoscopy tower assembly station.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; taxpayer portal: SITIO (Sistema Integrado de Información Tributaria) at dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first obtain a Panama Tax Identification Number (RUC) by appointing a resident agent (agente residente) and registering the entity with the Registro Único de Contribuyentes through the DGI, submitting certified articles of incorporation (escritura), proof of registered agent appointment, notarized identification of directors and beneficiary, and a local address; the RUC is issued before opening a local bank account or applying for an importer/exporter code (código de exportador/importador) via the DGI and Aduanas de Panamá.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Panama; entities are classified based on the territorial source of income, under which only Panamanian-source income is subject to ISR; taxpayers may elect the small taxpayer regime (régimen de pequeños contribuyentes) if gross turnover does not exceed the statutory threshold, and may elect for the simplified VAT payment scheme (cuota fija) when applicable; hybrid entity availability arises through Private Interest Foundation (PIF) flexibility, enabling perpetual existence and separate patrimony with foundation council control, but no pass-through election is available for Panama corporate income tax purposes other than the transparent treatment of partnerships and trusts under specific statutory rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The DGI mandates VAT registration for any person or entity whose taxable transactions exceed USD 36,000 annually or whose estimated taxable transactions exceed this threshold; businesses selling exoneration-listed goods or providing services are nonetheless required to register and obtain the RUC and VAT authorization before invoicing.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama operates a phased electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) regime administered by the DGI, requiring generation of XML invoices with digital signature and immediate transmission through the SITIO platform; authorized taxpayers, including exporters and importers, must use DGI-authorised technological issuers (emisores tecnológicos), comply with schema validation (schema v1.0 / extension for ITBMS 7%), include the 'CF' (Comprobante Fiscal) electronic invoice code and AUI code, and transmit in real time; businesses over the VAT registration threshold must issue e-invoices with a printed or digital fiscal stamp (papel sellado / timbre fiscal) and transmit data in batches no later than 24 hours for top-tier obligors.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Panama territorial taxation zero-rates exports of goods and services when the transaction is destined to a buyer abroad and income is sourced outside Panama; for ITBMS purposes, exports are subject to zero rate where the seller demonstrates that goods physically leave Panama under a customs export procedure (exportación definitiva) or services are provided to non-residents for use abroad, and the service is not connected with Panamanian real property or Panamanian-situs benefits; VAT registrants may claim input VAT refunds based on purchase invoices properly issued to the exporter's RUC, and refunds of ITBMS credits are subject to a 13% retention/withholding regime on the reimbursable balance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Formulario Único de Aduanas (Customs Export Declaration / DUA) duly accepted by Aduanas de Panamá
Bill of Lading (original or electronic B/L evidencing departure from Panamanian port)
Commercial invoice with RUC and export code of the exporter
Contract or purchase order from non-resident customer
Certificate of Origin (where applicable for tariff/vat relief)
Bank transfer receipt evidencing inward payment (comprobante de remesa)
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the Panamanian bank for the credits received
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to DGI audit review requiring full documentary provenance; false zero-rating invoicing, use of forged export documents, under-declared taxes, or failure to remit export proceeds within 180 days of the transaction may trigger assessment of the 7% ITBMS with additions up to 100% of the unpaid tax, surcharge of 1% per month (or 10% on provisional calculations), plus administrative fines of up to five times the annual net taxable amount for serious noncompliance (DGI penalty scale) and criminal tax fraud sanctions of 2 to 5 years imprisonment where evasion exceeds the statutory criminal threshold; PIF directors and resident agents signing false export declarations may be jointly liable and subjected to cancellation of the exporter code and RUC based on the DGI's investigative rulings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the competent banking and AML/CFT supervisor; Banco Nacional de Panamá operates the national clearinghouse and administers ACH Panamá. There is no central bank exercising monetary policy because Panama is fully dollarized, with the U.S. dollar as legal tender and the Balboa as a book-keeping unit at a 1:1 parity; exchange-rate and monetary-policy functions are effectively delegated to the U.S. Federal Reserve.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully convertible, dollarized system with no exchange controls on either current-account or capital-account transactions. Capital injections, trade payments, hedging transactions and profit remittances may be executed freely without central-bank approval. The only remittance hurdle is fiscal: a 10% definitive dividend/distribution withholding tax applies to Panama-source profits distributed by a local payor to non-resident beneficiaries (5% for dividends paid on securities registered with the Panama Stock Exchange), and the payor must evidence tax compliance before remittance. Distributions from foreign-source assets held by a Private Interest Foundation fall outside Panama territorial taxation and are not subject to withholding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory FX surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Panama, as the USD is local legal tender and no central bank exists. Exporters of medical devices under ISIC 3250 must comply with documentary and customs discipline: file the export customs declaration (DUA) through the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) electronic platform at or prior to exit, maintain active export registration with the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) and the single window for foreign trade, and hold a sanitary export permit / sanitary registration from the Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas (DNFD) of the Ministerio de Salud. Export proceeds may be retained in any domestic or foreign USD account without conversion or repatriation obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Specialized Foundation Trade and Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary treasury or clearing venue, MEDIUM as an auxiliary receivable-collection channel. Panama does not issue EU-style electronic-money-institution (EMI) licenses; payment service providers must be authorized by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá under Law 23 of 2015 and the SBP fintech facilitation framework. Unlicensed offshore EMIs generally decline Private Interest Foundations due to complex beneficial-ownership analysis and cannot lawfully execute settlement, escrow, or trade-LC functions for a Panamanian entity. A locally authorized fintech wallet may accept export receivables only if balances are swept daily to the Tier-1 bank account, while escrow, LC, and mass-disbursement flows must remain exclusively on the SWIFT banking rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the statutory default. The beneficial owners, foundation-council members, and designated signatories must appear in person before the bank's Compliance Officer for the initial KYC interview under SBP Agreement 03-2015. Remote video opening is permitted only when the client is referred by a regulated financial institution subject to equivalent KYC standards, supported by notarized and apostilled attestations, and accompanied by the appointment of a Panama-licensed resident agent or the grant of a notarial General Power of Attorney to a Panama-based representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation substance opacity: account officer challenges the absence of local payroll, physical office, and audited financial statements for the Private Interest Foundation legal vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the notarized and apostilled Foundation Charter registered at the Registro Público; council minutes approving the treasury mandate and manufacturing business scope; current certificate of existence (Copia Certificada); a commercial substance memorandum identifying the Panama premises, resident agent, and underlying endoscope-manufacturing operating company; interim management accounts; Aviso de Operación (tax registration); tax-compliance certificate; and a signed declaration describing the territorial sourcing of revenues.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction or PEP flag on a non-resident founder or beneficiary, triggering enhanced due diligence and possible account refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit individual PEP and sanctions questionnaires for each protected party; sworn declarations of lawful fund origin; negative public-record and adverse-media investigation reports from a professional discovery provider with audit trail; two independent bank or trade reference letters; a licensed Panamanian attorney's legal opinion confirming that no party is an exposed person under SBP Agreement 03-2015; GAFILAT/FATF-compliant screening results with date and time stamps; and, if a PEP is identified, a senior-management-approved acceptance report with an enhanced monitoring plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of escrow-injection funds: large inward MT103 credits arrive as personal savings or family funds without documentary trade or capital linkage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a pre-credit source-of-funds book containing the endowment or contribution agreement; underlying export contracts and commercial invoices for laparoscopy-tower sales; LC records and bills of lading; three months of prior bank statements of the remitting party; sanctioned-entity screening certificates; certified English and Spanish translations of all foreign documents; and a signed instruction identifying each inbound credit as capital contribution, intercompany loan, or trade advance with matching purpose text.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Speculative-hedging concern: treasury requests for leveraged FX instruments trigger the SBP suitability review and correspondent-bank scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a treasury policy manual evidencing risk-only hedging matched to JPY, EUR, and CNH accounts payables for German optical components and Japanese 4K sensors; board-approved dealing mandates; executed ISDA/CSA confirmations; and a written declaration that uncovered, leveraged, or speculative positions are prohibited under the bank's suitability policy and SBP margin rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use or end-use concern: 4K rigid endoscope technology is temporarily misclassified as controlled optics, delaying payment credits and LC confirmation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble a regulatory defense dossier comprising the MINSA sanitary registration; ISIC 3250 / NAICS 339112 classification statement; HS 9018.90 line-item declaration confirming finished low-risk laparoscopic endoscopes; CE-mark and FDA 510(k) evidence where applicable; end-user declarations; OFAC and EU dual-use line-item certification; and a signed compliance undertaking to notify the bank of any embargoed destination or sanctioned end-user within 48 hours.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route all equity endowments and intercompany capital injections by SWIFT MT103/MT202 referencing the Foundation Charter article authorizing the capital contribution or escrow agreement, with purpose text such as 'Capital Injection - Foundation Endowment' or 'Trade Advance - Export Contract INV-XXXX'. USD funds arrive through the sending bank's New York correspondent via Fedwire/CHIPS and are credited to the Panama account only after tests against the foundation's pre-approved counterparty list and source-of-funds file. No exchange-control approval or import certificate is required in Panama; any mismatch between the remitter profile and the declared purpose will trigger a freeze and a Suspicious Transaction Report under Law 23 of 2015. Export proceeds from buyers of laparoscopy towers should be remitted as 'Export Proceeds - Invoice XYZ' with the commercial invoice and DUA transmitted through the same banking channel for auditability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for imported optical components and electronic subassemblies are executed by MT103 in USD through the Panama bank's New York correspondent to the beneficiary bank. For large or recurring purchases of German optical components and Japanese CMOS sensors, the recommended rail is an irrevocable Letter of Credit issued under UCP600, available by sight or by 30-90 day usance draft, and confirmed by the beneficiary bank in the supplying country. Required LC documents comprise the commercial invoice, airway bill, insurance certificate, and English-language CE/FDA certificates where applicable. Domestic USD transfers among Panamanian counterparties clear through ACH Panamá operated by Banco Nacional de Panamá, while cross-border high-value payments achieve finality on the U.S. Federal Reserve network and CHIPS. No Panama clearing or exchange-control approval is needed for outbound disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR vanilla FX spot and outright forwards for German optical-component payables, tenor up to 12 months, executed bilaterally under an ISDA 1992 master agreement with an SBP-licensed bank or its international dealing desk.
USD/JPY and USD/CNH cross-currency swaps for multi-year procurement of 4K sensors and camera modules, matched to underlying import-currency exposure and net-settled in USD.

Non-deliverable forwards (USD/CNH, USD/KRW) permitted via a licensed international broker as an OTC overlay for currencies without local deliverability, with margin collateral held in a USD escrow account.

European-style plain vanilla USD/EUR and USD/JPY options for contingent capital-expenditure conversion, with premiums payable in USD and settlement by physical delivery of the underlying counterpart currency.

All instruments must be documented against underlying trade exposure; uncovered, leveraged, or speculative positions are prohibited under SBP suitability standards and the bank's internal dealing policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Tax (Tasa Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado) – mandatory payment to preserve legal existence under Law 25 of 1995 (as amended).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) – online payment portal 'Tasas'.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable each calendar year from January 1 through March 31; newly created foundations must pay within the first three months following the date of inscription in the Public Registry (prorated).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge on the unpaid tax; persistent non-payment for two or more consecutive fiscal years causes loss of 'buena gestión' (good standing) and may lead to administrative strike-off/dissolution of the foundation by the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation – 'Declaración de Beneficiario Final' under Law 12 of 2017 and Executive Decree regulating the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) – Final Beneficial Owner Registry Section (Sistema de Beneficiarios Finales).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing of the UBO declaration at incorporation, yearly Q1 confirmatory filing (aligned with the franchise-tax window), and mandatory updates within fifteen (15) days of any change in direct or indirect ownership structure (ownership threshold of 10% or more).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory monetary fines of B/.100.00 to B/.5,000.00 per infraction; the Public Registry may suspend issuance of certificates of good standing, block corporate acts, and report the foundation to the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) for AML risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Appointment / Re-appointment Protocol of Foundation Council Members, Protector and Registered Agent – verification of the docket (expediente) and payment of any ledger or certificate fees to maintain the legal standing of the foundation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (for amendments and certified extracts) and the Fondation's licensed Resident Agent (licensed under Law 25/1995 and Law 2 of 2011).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the anniversary of incorporation: review of registers, confirmation of the legal status of all Council members, and renewal of the registered-agent engagement before any lapse occurs; documented consents must be kept in the minute book.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unmaintained agency relationship or lapsed registered agent results in a notice of non-compliance, disqualification of the foundation from registering acts, fees for reactivation, and administrative strike-off risk if left unresolved for more than one fiscal year.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Private Interest Foundations are not subject to a compulsory annual audit for their statutory filings; an independent audit ('dictamen de Contador Público Autorizado') is mandatory for Panamanian commercial taxpayers whose gross taxable income exceeds B/.1,000,000.00 per fiscal year, and may also be contractually required by lenders, insurers, or the foundation charter for a foundation operating a medical-device manufacturing business.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Normas Internacionales de Información Financiera (IFRS/NIIF) – as adopted by the College of Public Accountants of Panama and the DGI for general-purpose financial statements; simplified (cash-basis or IFRS for SMEs) may be used in the foundation's internal books where no statutory consolidation is required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation Council must keep a classified UBO register identifying every individual holding, directly or indirectly, 10% or more of voting rights or economic interests, the founder, protector, council members and designated beneficiaries; the register must be attested by the registered agent and uploaded to the Public Registry's Sistema de Beneficiarios Finales each year, with amendment filings due within 15 days of any transfer of foundation rights or changes in the beneficiary chain.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Beneficiaries (Registro de Miembros y Beneficiarios)
Register of Foundation Council Members and Protector
Minute Book and Foundation Charter (Estatuto), including amendments

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat corporate income tax (ISR – Impuesto sobre la Renta) imposed under the Panama Fiscal Code on the net taxable income of legal entities for all income sourced within Panama or derived from Panama permanent establishments.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial tax regime: 0% tax on genuinely foreign-source income; 0% to 5% preferential rates for qualified medical-technology manufacturers established in accredited free-zone or industrial-processing zones (e.g., Panama Pacifico) benefiting from investment-promotion laws; 100% deductibility of direct manufacturing costs, depreciation of medical production equipment, and R&D-related fixed-asset amortization; tax-exempt reorganization provisions; no wealth or capital gains tax on shares where the underlying asset is foreign-source.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 101 (Declaración Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed through the DGI's mandatory electronic portal 'T@-P-2' (Sistema de Declaraciones Electrónicas); payment of the resulting tax via ACH/debit settlement registered in the 'Portal de Contribuyentes'.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year (31 March for calendar-year taxpayers); the DGI extends the sunset deadline only when the due date falls on a non-business day; transitional quarterly estimated prepayment obligations apply when gross revenue exceeds USD 1,500,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RUC number, resident agent reference, and foundation registration certificate ID of the PIF or its operating entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Since the PIF is non-resident-owned, enter the foreign beneficial owner's information in the supplementary 'Beneficiary Identification' annex; the resident agent must certify the foundation's active registry status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2a (Gross Worldwide Income – Panama Source Only)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue derived from Panama-source commercial/industrial activities, i.e., surgical endoscope manufacturing sales, assembly services, and related warehouse sales completed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude all foreign-source manufacturing income under the territorial rule; attach a notarized certificate of foreign activities only when the PIF conducts assembly abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares income exempt by statute: foreign-source revenue, free-zone export earnings, capital gains on foreign securities, and non-business investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF beneficially owning the endoscopy IP and licensing it abroad may claim full exemption, but should attach the license agreements and evidence of decision-making outside Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8c (Deductions – Cost of Sales and Operating Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct materials for laparoscopy tower production (rigid scopes, 4K imaging sensors), payroll, depreciation of CNC/sterilization equipment, freight, and technical royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only if supported by invoices and contracts with economic substance; intra-group component purchases require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source income minus statutory deductions and any net operating loss carryforward (max 5 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 5-year loss carryforward only for losses previously declared and accepted by the DGI in an audited tax loss certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 25% flat statutory rate to Net Taxable Income; no graduated band applies to this manufacturing operation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foundation's only income is foreign-source dividends from its SA operating subsidiary, Box 20 is completed with '0' and the zero-tax election is justified in the comments annex.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fine of up to USD 5,000 plus a 10% surcharge on the tax due; additional interest of 3% per month (or fraction of a month) compounded on the unpaid ISR; failure to file after DGI formal notice carries double-surcharge recalculation, automatic embargo of bank accounts, and publication on the delinquent taxpayer registry; criminal liability for false declarations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Estimated Advance Payment Module – 'Pago a Cuenta del Impuesto sobre la Renta' rendered electronically through T@-P-2 (quarterly electronic declarations for large taxpayers above USD 1,500,000 gross income).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly advance returns and prepayments due by 30 April, 31 July, 31 October, and 31 January, calculated on the basis of the prior final return; the DGI fixes the final annual prepayment adjustment in the Form 101 cycle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select fiscal quarter; manufacturing taxpayers report projected Panama-source revenue adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owed amounts are computed by the resident agent using the DGI assessment formula; no treasury withholding applies to foreign-source proceeds credited through Swift LC/TT rails.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Maps accumulated losses deductible against the quarter's estimated tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss offsets apply only where the PIF holds an approved loss plan and cannot be used to shelter income of a separate SA subsidiary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment of quarterly advance amounts: 2% monthly interest surcharge plus re-quantification of the annual tax with the 10% fidelity fine; persistent delinquency triggers the suspension of import/export customs permits and mandatory prepayment indexation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding on dividends distributed by a Panama corporation out of profits not previously subjected to corporate income tax; 5% reduced withholding where the distributing company elects the credit-method (taxed-account) treatment and retains the relevant ISR paid; distributions by a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) are statutorily outside the dividend withholding regime when the foundation holds only exempt/foreign-source assets, but once the PIF realizes Panama-source commercial profits, the distribution to a foreign beneficiary is re-characterized as a deemed dividend and subjected to the 10% rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply DTA relief, the foreign beneficiary must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) in the counterparty jurisdiction; (ii) submit the TRC with evidence of beneficial ownership to the paying entity before the distribution; (iii) have the Panamanian paying entity file the DGI beneficial-ownership declaration and supporting DTA form electronically within 15 days of payment; (iv) respond to substantive review by the DGI within 30 days; where relieved, the DWT is reduced to the applicable treaty rate (typically 0%–5%) and the excess withheld is refundable through the Form 101 annual credit procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Panama-source royalties for technology, patents, trademarks, or industrial processes paid to foreign related parties: 15% final withholding (paid by the payer); statutory Panama-source interest paid to foreign lenders: 12.5% final withholding; treaty-reduced rates: 0%–10% for royalties and 0%–5% for interest under Panama's DTAs with Mexico, UAE, Spain, UK, Netherlands, Qatar, South Korea, Singapore, Italy, Luxembourg, and Barbados, subject to the beneficiary's active conduct and no treaty-shopping arrangement.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (Informe Local) mandatory when cross-border related-party transactions, including component purchases, royalty payments, intercompany loans, or revenue-sharing for 4K endoscopy hardware, exceed USD 1,000,000 per fiscal year; Master File (Informe Maestro) and documentation consolidation required when the PIF/group consolidated gross revenue exceeds USD 5,000,000; Country-by-Country reporting applies if the ultimate parent group's consolidated revenue is USD 750,000,000 or more; amounts are in Panamanian Balboas (PAB) which are pegged 1:1 to the USD.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) – preferred for rigid endoscope component sales
Cost Plus Method (CPM) – preferred for contract manufacturing of laparoscopy towers
Profit Split Method (PSM) – applied for joint IP ownership of surgical imaging software
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations apply to PIFs, corporations, and hybrid entities conducting 'relevant activities' (including manufacturing, distribution, and pure holding of intangible assets). A PIF commercially manufacturing surgical laparoscopy towers must demonstrate in each fiscal year: (i) physical premises in Panama; (ii) resident employees commensurate with the activity; (iii) locally incurred operating expenditures; (iv) board meetings and decision-making for procurement, quality control, and export sales occurring in Panama; and (v) statutory books and records kept in Panama. The DGI requires submission of an annual substance attestation with the Form 101 package; a pure-asset-holding PIF is exempt from commercial substance only if it does not carry on any Panama trade or business.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of Panama-source manufacturing revenue from Form 101, fraudulent underreporting of 4K endoscope export sales, falsification of invoices for raw material inputs, or creation of artificial tax-loss documents without underlying production.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of two to five times the evaded tax; imprisonment of 2 to 5 years; automatic nullity of the false tax declaration; 3% monthly surcharge compounding on the evaded ISR; cancellation of the taxpayer's RUC and mandatory closure of the commercial establishment; inclusion in the DGI's Public Defaulter list and loss of all government procurement rights.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the resident agent, and the financial officer face joint and several civil liability for the evaded tax plus penalties; the DGI and Public Ministry may impose travel bans, freeze corporate and personal bank accounts, request international asset seizure through mutual legal assistance, and obtain personal bankruptcy orders for the officers who signed the fraudulent return.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF is registered as the owner of the surgical endoscopy manufacturing operation but maintains no employees, no physical production premises, no local board meetings, and no operational decision-making, using nominee directors solely to channel profits through Panama without substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to USD 750,000 per fiscal year under the Economic Substance Regulations; deregistration of the PIF from the Foundation Registry; disqualification and personal sanction of the resident agent; re-integration of all foreign-source profits as Panama-source income; refusal by the DGI to honor treaty benefits; and revocation of the manufacturing license granted by the Ministry of Health.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers are personally liable for unpaid taxes on re-characterized income; courts may impose civil restitution equal to the diverted profits; travel bans and prohibitions from acting as director of any Panama legal entity for up to 10 years; criminal money-laundering charges where the artificial structure was used to conceal the true beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF/SA imports laparoscopy tower components from a non-resident affiliate at artificially inflated prices, licenses endoscopy IP into Panama with excessive royalty rates, or fails to create its Local File/Master File when related-party transactions exceed USD 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI full or partial re-characterization of the transactions at arm's length; assessment of the resulting additional ISR at 25% plus 3% monthly interest; a specific penalty equal to 5%–15% of the undocumented transaction value; potential double taxation without treaty MAP access where the adjustment is unilateral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or signed intercompany agreements outside arm's-length parameters are personally liable for the tax differential in the event of corporate insolvency or liquidation; travel bans and seizure of personal real estate may be imposed during the coercive collection phase, and criminal liability arises when the transfer pricing documentation is found to be knowingly falsified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the final beneficial owner with Panama's Registro de Beneficiarios Finales within 30 days of the PIF's creation; concealment of the ultimate shareholder behind clear-form nominees while receiving Swift LC/Wire (TT) proceeds from medical device sales; processing of export payments through non-banking channels or with mismatched invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to USD 1,000,000 per infraction under Law 23 of 2015 (AML), Law 254 of 2021 (Beneficial Ownership Registry), and the Criminal Code's money-laundering provisions; administrative seizure and freezing of Swift LC/Wire funds; cancellation of the foundation's registration; denial of banking licenses and corporate accounts; referral to the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) for criminal prosecution with imprisonment of 5 to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face personal criminal liability, civil liability for laundering proceeds derived from the underlying fiscal offense, inclusion on international denial-of-benefit lists, extradition risk through Interpol red notices, and personal travel bans reinforced by the Panamanian Immigration Authority.
